title_original: Securing AI Agents from Discovery to Runtime: Check Point on Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise
description: AI agents are moving into production fast. They read enterprise data, call tools, and take actions across business systems. That creates a new problem: an agent can be fully authenticated and authorized and still be manipulated into doing the wrong thing. Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterprise gives enterprises a central control plane for agents. Check Point extends that control plane with AI-specific risk assessment and real-time, context-aware protection. This post details where Check Point integrates and what it looks like for a security team. Google Cloud’s direction with agent orchestration, registries, and gateway layers signals a clear design pattern: centralized AI […]The postSecuring AI Agents from Discovery to Runtime: Check Point on Google Cloud’s Gemini Enterpriseappeared first onCheck Point Blog.

title_original: Inside the Q3 2026 Brand Phishing Report: Microsoft Now Accounts for One in Three Brand Impersonation
description: In Q3 2026, Microsoft was the most impersonated brand in phishing attacks, accounting for 33% of all brand impersonation attempts tracked by Check Point Research, up from 23% in Q2. Attackers favor Microsoft because stolen Microsoft credentials can unlock an entire corporate environment, including email, files and collaboration tools, while many of the other top brands mainly lead to personal accounts. Apple, Google, LinkedIn and Amazon completed the top five, and together these brands made up more than half of all attempts, showing how heavily attackers lean on a small group of trusted names.
